name: Grand Foyer
read: The street doors close behind you on a long theatre foyer, where a worn red carpet runs between four stone pillars. Velvet rope posts stand in a crooked line toward a ticket booth against the east wall, where a single lamp still burns behind the glass. Torn playbills cover the floor around a toppled umbrella stand and a small round table with a lamp on it. The playbills all show the same smiling puppet over the words: The Gilded Thimble Presents.
notes:
The front of the Gilded Thimble Playhouse, shut for a year. The lamp in the ticket booth has burned all that time without oil; Tangle keeps it lit so that passers-by think the house is still open. The playbills are for Ambrose Quill's last show, The Dance Without Strings. The rest of the playhouse is dark unless a room says otherwise.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Rehearsal Hall (4, door and arch), Auditorium (2, door and open passage), Costume Wardrobe (5, door and arch), Stage Door (3, door), Prop Store (9, door), Doll Parlour (6, door and arch), Understage Cellar (15, door, stairs and arch). The double doors in the middle of the north side lead back out to the street. The door in the middle of the east side opens onto a short passage: to the north it ends at an arch into the south side of the Rehearsal Hall, to the east an open passage leads into the Auditorium, and to the south an arch opens into the north side of the Costume Wardrobe. The door in the south side, east of the middle, opens onto a long back passage running south, with doors off it into the Stage Door, the Costume Wardrobe and the Prop Store; at its south end it turns east toward the Doll Parlour and the stairs down to the Understage Cellar.

name: Auditorium
read: Rows of red velvet seats face north across this small auditorium, and in almost every seat sits a porcelain doll in its best clothes, facing the dark where the stage should be. Programmes lie scattered in the aisles, and many seat cushions have been gnawed open, their stuffing pulled out across the floor. Tiny clockwork mice sit among the stuffing. As you watch, one turns its tin head toward you, and somewhere under the seats a hundred tiny keys begin to wind.
notes:
Quill built the clockwork mice for a children's matinee. With the house shut, they have run wild and nest inside the seat cushions. The dolls in the seats are empty shells, dressed as an audience by Tangle; they never move and can be ignored.

Encounter (Power Level 8)

5 Tinwhisker Swarms nest in the seats. They pour out when a creature walks down an aisle and fight until destroyed. A swarm's space is underfoot: a creature that enters it may be knocked Prone, and a swarm that climbs onto a face can Blind its target, as the stat block describes. The swarms are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Grand Foyer (1, open passage and door), Rehearsal Hall (4, open passage and arch), Costume Wardrobe (5, open passage and arch), Green Room (7, door), Doll Parlour (6, door), Ventriloquist's Parlour (8, arch). The open passage in the middle of the west side leads to a short passage: west to a door into the Grand Foyer, north to an arch into the Rehearsal Hall, and south to an arch into the Costume Wardrobe. The door in the middle of the north side opens into the Green Room. The door in the middle of the south side opens into the Doll Parlour. The arch at the north end of the east side opens into the south end of the west side of the Ventriloquist's Parlour.

name: Stage Door
read: This small back entrance holds a doorman's stool and a small desk with a sign-in book lying open on it. A coat rack stands by the double doors in the north wall, and a stagehand's apron hangs on a hook beside it. A lantern lies on its side on the floor among a few stacked crates, its glass cracked.
notes:
The rear entrance of the playhouse, where actors and stagehands came and went. The last names in the sign-in book are those of the stage crew; none of them signed out. The apron belonged to Tobin Marsh, a stagehand who vanished on the last night of the last show.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in the pocket of the dead stagehand's apron.

Exits: Prop Store (9, arch), back passage (door) to the Grand Foyer (1), Costume Wardrobe (5), Doll Parlour (6) and Understage Cellar (15). The double doors in the middle of the north side lead out to the alley behind the playhouse. The door in the middle of the east side opens onto the long back passage: north it ends at a door into the south side of the Grand Foyer, and south it passes a door into the Costume Wardrobe and a door into the Prop Store before turning east toward the Doll Parlour and the stairs down to the Understage Cellar. The arch at the west end of the south side opens into the Prop Store.

name: Rehearsal Hall
read: The wooden floor of this hall is covered in chalk circles and crosses marking dance positions. A mirror runs the length of the west wall and a barre runs along the east wall, with a piano stool and a few music stands between them. Limp marionettes hang from hooks along the walls, their strings rising into the dark above, and as you enter the strings draw tight. Out in the passage to the south, a little sand lies spilled on the floor.
notes:
Quill's dancers rehearsed here. Tangle has strung four of the marionettes with stolen souls, and they still practise the steps of the last show.

Encounter (Power Level 9)

4 Marionette Dancers hang from the hooks. They drop and attack when a creature crosses the chalk marks, and fight until destroyed. Each hangs from strings and can leap 30 feet on them. A creature can cut a dancer's strings with an attack against AC 15 that deals 10 Slashing damage; the dancer then has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

Talking. The dancers want to rehearse and fear blades near their strings. A character who steps onto the chalk marks and dances the steps (DC 15 Charisma (Performance) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check) keeps them dancing instead of fighting for as long as the dance goes on. A character who holds a blade to a dancer's strings and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Intimidation) check makes all four climb back to their hooks and hang still.

Trap: Falling Counterweight

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 10 feet of corridor halfway between the Rehearsal Hall's south arch and the junction to the south.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices a frayed rope overhead holding a heavy sandbag, and sand on the floor beneath it.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 bludgeoning]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, pinned under the sandbag until it or an ally uses an action and succeeds on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
  • Disarm or avoid: Cut the rope from outside the area, or prop the bag in place (DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check).
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Stage Wings (11, arch and door), Scenery Dock (14, open passage and arch), Green Room (7, open passage and arch), Grand Foyer (1, arch and door), Auditorium (2, arch and open passage), Costume Wardrobe (5, arch). The arch at the south end of the west side opens onto a short passage west that ends at a door into the middle of the east side of the Stage Wings. The open passage in the middle of the north side leads to a passage north and then east to a junction: north from it an arch opens into the Scenery Dock, and south from it a passage runs down to an arch into the Green Room. The arch in the middle of the south side opens onto the trapped corridor south, which ends at a junction: a door west into the Grand Foyer, an open passage east into the Auditorium, and an arch south into the Costume Wardrobe.

name: Costume Wardrobe
read: Racks of costumes line the east and west walls of this long room: ball gowns, jesters' motley and soldiers' coats, all thick with dust. Dressmaker's dummies stand between hat boxes, and a sewing table holds spools of thread and a pincushion. Against the middle of the south wall sits a small iron-bound strongbox. Its lock is bright and new, and around it the dust on the floor has been disturbed.
notes:
The playhouse wardrobe. Lord Ashgrove's sister, Mirabel, sang in Quill's last show; her dressing things were packed into the strongbox after she vanished. Tangle had the box trapped so that whoever came looking for her would be poisoned.

Trap: Needle in the Strongbox

  • Trigger: a creature opens the iron-bound strongbox against the middle of the south wall (the squares in front of it).
  • Find: DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) finds a hair-fine needle hidden in the keyhole.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam or remove the needle (DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools).
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: in the strongbox, the Ashgrove Silk Scarf (a pale blue silk scarf with the Ashgrove crest of a grey heron, Mirabel's) and 300 gp. The scarf matches the one worn by a Porcelain Doll in the Doll Parlour (room 6), and Lord Ashgrove (room 10) knows it at once.

Exits: Grand Foyer (1, arch and door), Auditorium (2, arch and open passage), Rehearsal Hall (4, arch), back passage (door) to the Stage Door (3) and Prop Store (9), Doll Parlour (6, door and arch), Understage Cellar (15, door, stairs and arch). The arch in the middle of the north side opens onto a short passage north: a door west into the Grand Foyer, an open passage east into the Auditorium, and on north to the trapped corridor and the Rehearsal Hall (see room 4). The door in the west side, south of the middle, opens onto the long back passage, with doors into the Stage Door, the Prop Store and the Grand Foyer. The door in the east side, south of the middle, opens onto a short passage east to a corridor: north it ends at an arch into the Doll Parlour, and south it leads to the stairs down to the Understage Cellar.

name: Doll Parlour
read: Shelves of porcelain dolls line every wall of this parlour, rows of painted faces turned toward the door. A child-sized tea table is set with tiny cups beside a rocking chair, a dollhouse and lace doilies. A few cracked doll heads lie on the floor. Four larger dolls sit among the others, and one of them wears a pale blue silk scarf. Each time you look away and back, the dolls are a little closer.
notes:
Quill's showroom, where finished dolls waited for buyers. Four of the dolls hold souls stolen by Tangle. One of them is Mirabel Ashgrove, Lord Ashgrove's sister; she wears a scarf that matches the Ashgrove Silk Scarf from room 5.

Encounter (Power Level 10)

4 Porcelain Dolls. A doll has a speed of 0 while any enemy can see it, so the dolls only creep forward when nobody is looking at them; a doll that is looked at goes still and harmless. When a doll is destroyed it shatters into sharp shards, as its stat block describes. The dolls are not intelligent enough to bargain with.

Mirabel. A character who notices the blue scarf (DC 13 Wisdom (Perception), or automatically if a character carries the Ashgrove Silk Scarf or Lord Ashgrove is with the party) can spare that doll. Once it is seen for what it is, the Mirabel doll is not hostile: it does not move or attack, and it lifts its head toward the scarf. Cutting the Soul Spool (room 12) frees her.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Auditorium (2, door), Toymaker's Workshop (10, gate), Costume Wardrobe (5, arch and door), Understage Cellar (15, arch, stairs and arch), back passage (arch). The door in the middle of the north side opens into the Auditorium. The iron gate at the north end of the east side opens into the middle of the west side of the Toymaker's Workshop. The arch in the middle of the south side opens onto a corridor south: a short passage west off it ends at a door into the Costume Wardrobe, and at its south end it meets the back passage, which runs east to stairs down to the Understage Cellar and west toward the Prop Store, the Stage Door and the Grand Foyer.

name: Green Room
read: A worn sofa faces a small table set with tea things and a little brass music box. A dressing screen painted with roses stands in one corner, and a mirror ringed with cold candles hangs beside it. An old costume trunk sits against the wall, its lid closed.
notes:
The actors waited here before they went on. The tea things were left out on the last night of the last show. The music box plays the waltz from The Dance Without Strings; the Prima Marionette (room 10) knows it.

No encounter.

Treasure: Quill's Music Box on the table, and a Potion of Healing in the costume trunk. A character who plays the music box while dancing with the Prima Marionette has Advantage on the check (see room 10).

Exits: Auditorium (2, door), Ventriloquist's Parlour (8, arch), Scenery Dock (14, arch and arch), Rehearsal Hall (4, arch and open passage). The door in the middle of the south side opens into the Auditorium. The arch at the south end of the east side opens into the middle of the west side of the Ventriloquist's Parlour. The arch in the middle of the north side opens onto a corridor north to a junction: an arch north opens into the Scenery Dock, and a passage west and south ends at an open passage into the Rehearsal Hall.

name: Ventriloquist's Parlour
read: Three small chairs stand in a row on a low platform in this large dressing room, and in each sits a wooden dummy in a little velvet suit. A dressing table holds a mirror ringed with candles, beside a hat stand and open trunks full of wooden heads and spare limbs. In an armchair facing the platform slumps the body of a thin man in a dress coat, with glass lenses over his eyes. As you enter, all three dummies turn their heads toward you, and the man's voice says: Ah. An audience at last.
notes:
The dressing room of Ambrose Quill, puppet master of the Gilded Thimble. The body in the armchair is Quill himself, dead for months; Tangle made him her ventriloquist's mouthpiece when he tried to stop her. His three dummies still speak in his voice.

Encounter (Power Level 11)

3 Ventriloquist's Dummy constructs. Their leader is the middle dummy, Mister Pennywhistle. A dummy can throw its voice to lure a character away, turn an attack aside onto another creature (It was him!), and put words in a caster's mouth, as the stat block describes. They fight until destroyed, but they would rather be watched.

Talking. The dummies want applause and a performance, and they fear an empty house. If the party gives them an audience and a show, one character makes a DC 15 Charisma (Performance) check (Advantage if the others applaud). On a success the dummies are delighted: they do not attack, they let the party take what Quill carries, and in Quill's voice they tell his story, that Tangle lives in the fly loft and that her strings are tied off on the pin rail. On a failure by 5 or more they boo, and attack.

Treasure: Eyes of Charming over the eyes of Quill's body.

Exits: Green Room (7, arch), Auditorium (2, arch). The arch in the middle of the west side opens into the Green Room. The arch at the south end of the west side opens into the north end of the east side of the Auditorium.

name: Prop Store
read: Shelves of stage props line the walls of this small room: wooden swords, painted shields, a stuffed crocodile and a cardboard moon. Coils of rope lie on the floor. Along the shelf on the south wall stands a row of jack-in-the-box toys, each with a painted clown on its lid. The floor in front of them is scored with fine scratches.
notes:
The playhouse props, kept by the stage crew. Tangle has made the jack-in-the-box toys a guard of their own: each holds a clown on a spring with a knife in its hand.

Trap: Jack-in-the-Box Shelf

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 5-foot strip along the south wall, the whole 30 feet of it.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices tiny holes in the box lids and knife scratches on the floor in front of the shelf.
  • Effect: DC 16 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 piercing]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Wedge the lids shut (DC 16 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check), or walk along the north side of the room.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Stage Door (3, arch), back passage (door) to the Grand Foyer (1), Costume Wardrobe (5), Doll Parlour (6) and Understage Cellar (15). The arch at the west end of the north side opens into the Stage Door. The door in the middle of the east side opens onto the long back passage: north it passes doors into the Stage Door and the Costume Wardrobe and ends at the Grand Foyer, and south it turns east toward the Doll Parlour and the stairs down to the Understage Cellar.

name: Toymaker's Workshop
read: A lamp burns on one of the long workbenches that line the walls of this workshop, among carving tools, jars of paint and glue, and half-carved marionette limbs. Wood shavings cover the floor around a lathe. In the middle of the room a man in fine clothes sits in a tall chair, bound to it by puppet strings, and his hands are smooth, pale wood up to the wrists. A slender marionette in a ballerina's dress glides around him, its hand on his shoulder, as if they were dancing.
notes:
Quill's workshop. The man is Lord Edric Ashgrove, patron of the theatre, who came looking for his missing sister Mirabel. He is slowly turning to wood from the hands up. The marionette is The Prima Marionette, Tangle's favourite, and she keeps him as her dance partner. The workbench lamp gives light across the room.

Encounter (Power Level 11)

The Prima Marionette and 2 Marionette Dancers. The Prima Marionette is the commander: she gives orders to the dancers and calls an Encore, as her stat block describes. The dancers' strings can be cut as in room 4.

Talking. The Prima Marionette wants a partner who can out-dance her, and she fears Tangle. A character who asks her to dance and wins makes a DC 17 Charisma (Performance) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (Advantage with Quill's Music Box playing). On a success she lets Lord Ashgrove go. A DC 16 Charisma (Persuasion or Intimidation) check that reminds her Tangle throws away her old favourites makes her stand aside with her dancers and stay out of the fight in room 12. On a failure by 5 or more she attacks.

The noble. To free Lord Ashgrove, cut the strings (an action and a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, or 10 Slashing damage against AC 15; a failed check by 5 or more deals him 1d6 Slashing damage). Lesser Restoration or Remove Curse stops the wood spreading; cutting the Soul Spool (room 12) turns his hands back to flesh. He cannot fight with wooden hands. Freed, he tells the party that the Stage Manager's Key to the fire curtain is in the Scenery Dock (14), and that Tangle's strings are tied off on the pin rail in the fly loft. He asks them to find Mirabel.

Treasure: a Gray Bag of Tricks and a Potion of Healing on the workbench beside the lamp.

Exits: Doll Parlour (6, gate). The iron gate in the middle of the west side opens into the north end of the east side of the Doll Parlour.

name: Stage Wings
read: Coiled ropes and sandbag counterweights crowd the floor of these wings beside the stage. A lighting board of brass levers stands against one wall, near folded painted flats and a prompt desk with an open script. In the north wall, at its east end, an iron fire curtain blocks the way, locked fast. From somewhere above it comes a slow creak of rope, like something heavy shifting its weight.
notes:
The stage crew worked the scenery from here. The script on the prompt desk is for The Dance Without Strings; in its margins Quill has written, again and again, cut the strings. The iron fire curtain in the north wall is locked and leads to the Fly Loft (room 12). The Stage Manager's Key from the Scenery Dock (room 14) opens it. The lock can also be picked (DC 18 Dexterity check with thieves' tools) or the curtain forced up (DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check).

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Fly Loft (12, locked iron fire curtain), Fortune-Teller's Booth (13, open passage), Rehearsal Hall (4, door and arch). The locked iron fire curtain at the east end of the north side opens into the middle of the south side of the Fly Loft. The open passage in the middle of the west side leads into the Fortune-Teller's Booth. The door in the middle of the east side opens onto a short passage east that ends at an arch into the south end of the west side of the Rehearsal Hall.

name: The Fly Loft
read: You look down from the catwalk planks over the fly loft above the stage. A web of glittering threads covers the floor and gives a cold, pale light, and marionettes hang in it on strings like flies. Along the west wall, four thick ropes are tied off to the belaying pins of a wooden pin rail, and every thread in the room runs back to them. On a small table beside a pile of gold coins sits a large spool of shining thread. Above you something huge shifts on the ceiling: a cracked porcelain mask, and around it many long jointed wooden legs.
notes:
The end of the adventure. The thing on the ceiling is Mistress Tangle, the Spinner Above, the fey who gave Quill's puppets life. The spool is The Soul Spool: every soul she has taken is wound on it. The threads give pale light across the room.

Encounter (Power Level 12, final boss)

Mistress Tangle and 2 Marionette Dancers. Tangle is an Epic Boss: she clings to the ceiling, can make a character her puppet for a turn, and drops silk curtains that restrain, as her stat block describes. The dancers' strings can be cut as in room 4. If the Prima Marionette agreed to stand aside (room 10), she does not come.

Talking. Tangle wants new souls and fears the ropes on the pin rail being cut. She offers to let the party leave alive if one of them stays as her puppet; she keeps her word, but nothing frees the other souls. A character who stands at the pin rail with a blade on a rope and succeeds on a DC 18 Charisma (Intimidation) check makes her bargain: she releases Lord Ashgrove and Mirabel and lets the party go, if they leave the Soul Spool and never return. The Spool can only be cut free once she is dead.

The pin rail. Tangle's strings are tied off to four thick ropes on the wooden pin rail along the west wall. Each rope has AC 15, 25 Hit Points and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; or a creature can untie one as an action with a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. While at least one rope stands, Tangle has Epic Boss Resistance. Each rope cut drops one of her strung souls: each of the first two ropes cut makes one Marionette Dancer in the room collapse, with the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. When all four ropes are cut, Tangle loses Epic Boss Resistance, falls from the ceiling, takes [[/damage 4d10 bludgeoning]] damage and has the Prone condition.

The Soul Spool. Once Tangle is dead, a creature can cut the Spool free as an action. Every soul in the house is freed: the dolls and puppets go still, the missing townsfolk wake on the stage floor, Mirabel among them, and Lord Ashgrove's hands turn back to flesh.

Treasure: The Soul Spool (story item) on the small table, 600 gp in the pile beside it, and a Ring of Free Action on the hand of a marionette hanging in the web.

Exits: Stage Wings (11, locked iron fire curtain). The locked iron fire curtain in the middle of the south side opens into the east end of the north side of the Stage Wings.

name: Fortune-Teller's Booth
read: A velvet curtain hangs half open on this small booth, where a crystal ball glows violet on a little table. Behind it sits a life-size painted wooden dwarf with a long beard, holding a tarot deck in its hands. Red runs from the edges of the cards and drips onto the table, and loose cards lie scattered on the floor. A brass coin slot is set into the table in front of it.
notes:
Madame Fortuna, a fortune-teller automaton Quill built for the foyer, moved here by Tangle. The red on the deck is paint that never dries. The crystal ball gives a dim violet light.

No encounter.

The cards. A character who drops a coin into the slot is dealt one card; each character can draw once. Roll 1d4:

  • 1, The Sun. The character gains Heroic Inspiration.
  • 2, The Star. The character gains 10 Temporary Hit Points until the end of their next Long Rest.
  • 3, The Hanged Man. The character's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of their next Short or Long Rest.
  • 4, The Tower. The character has Disadvantage on their next attack roll.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Stage Wings (11, open passage). The open passage in the middle of the east side leads into the Stage Wings.

name: Scenery Dock
read: Painted backdrop flats stand stacked along the walls of this large store: a forest, a ballroom, a starry sky. A wooden castle set piece and a painted cardboard tree stand among rolls of canvas, buckets of paint and crates. On a stage manager's desk lies a ring of keys. A small wooden dummy sits on the desk beside it, legs dangling, and says brightly: Looking for something?
notes:
The old scenery of the playhouse is stored here. The dummy is Little Fitch, a spare dummy Quill never finished painting, and it guards the keys for Tangle. The two dolls stand hidden behind the flats, and the swarm nests in a roll of canvas.

Encounter (Power Level 10–11)

1 Ventriloquist's Dummy, 2 Porcelain Dolls and 1 Tinwhisker Swarm. The dummy throws its voice to lure characters behind the flats, where the dolls wait unseen; the dolls go still and harmless while looked at. The swarm attacks whoever reaches for the keys.

Talking. The dummy wants an audience. A character who performs for it and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Performance) check pleases it: it does not fight, and it warns the party that the dolls are behind the flats. The dolls and the swarm cannot be talked to and still attack.

Treasure: the Stage Manager's Key (story item; it opens the locked iron fire curtain between the Stage Wings and the Fly Loft) on the ring of keys on the desk, and a Rope of Climbing coiled in a crate beside it.

Exits: Green Room (7, arch and arch), Rehearsal Hall (4, arch and open passage). The arch in the middle of the south side opens onto a short corridor south to a junction: a passage south runs down to an arch into the Green Room, and a passage west and south ends at an open passage into the Rehearsal Hall.

name: Understage Cellar
read: Wooden support posts hold up the stage above this low cellar, among the gears and ropes of the old trapdoor machinery. Across the west half of the floor lies a cracked mosaic of comedy and tragedy masks, almost hidden under thick green and black mold. Broken crates lie scattered about. In the east corner, an iron strongbox lies half dug out of the earth floor.
notes:
The machinery under the stage raised and lowered actors through the trapdoors. The mosaic of the two masks is older than the playhouse; the mold has eaten most of it. Quill buried his savings here when the house began to empty.

Trap: Rot Mold

  • Trigger: a creature enters the moldy west half of the cellar, over the ruined mosaic (the west 20 feet of the room, wall to wall north to south).
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) or Wisdom (Perception) notices that the mold is thick and swollen, and that dead rats lie on it.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 necrotic]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.
  • Disarm or avoid: Burn it (any fire damage clears it), or walk along the east side of the room.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: 500 gp in the buried strongbox, with a Potion of Climbing.

Exits: Doll Parlour (6, arch, stairs and arch), back passage (arch and stairs) to the Costume Wardrobe (5), Prop Store (9), Stage Door (3) and Grand Foyer (1). The arch in the middle of the north side opens onto a short passage north to stairs that climb west to the back passage: from there a corridor runs north to an arch into the Doll Parlour, with a passage west off it to a door into the Costume Wardrobe, and the back passage runs west and north past the Prop Store, the Costume Wardrobe and the Stage Door to the Grand Foyer.
